name: Text Blaze
tagline: Browser-based text expander that turns short abbreviations into long templates, with form fields, dates and basic logic.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Keystroke-watching and string replacement is a solved problem, and an agent will give you a working Chrome extension with a snippet editor in one sitting. The hard part is everything after the happy path: Gmail's contenteditable, React controlled inputs that fight you, shadow DOM, iframes, sites that swallow synthetic input events. Text Blaze's actual product is years of per-site compatibility patches plus the template language with form fields, conditionals and date math. A personal build covers your own ten snippets on your own five sites just fine, and breaks silently on the sixth. Sync, mobile keyboards and shared team snippets are out of scope unless you want to build a backend too.
coreLoopDIY: A local Chrome extension that watches what you type in inputs and contenteditable fields, replaces trigger abbreviations with stored templates, and prompts you for fill-in fields before inserting.
requirements: Chrome or any Chromium browser you can load an unpacked extension into
Willingness to debug individual sites that refuse to accept programmatic text insertion
whatYouLose: Cross-device sync, including mobile keyboard expansion
Battle-tested compatibility with Gmail, Salesforce, LinkedIn and other hostile editors
The full template language: conditionals, formulas, remote data lookups, keyboard simulation
Shared team snippet folders and usage analytics
Someone else fixing it when Chrome changes extension APIs
moatNotes: The moat is a long tail of bug fixes against websites that each break text insertion in their own special way.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a text expander that works 90 percent of the time is worse than none at all: you learn to distrust it, you start checking every expansion, and the whole point evaporates. Paying buys the 10 percent, plus expansion on your phone and the ability to hand a snippet pack to a support team. For a solo user with a handful of snippets in a handful of apps, the local build genuinely holds up, and the OS-level text replacement built into macOS and Windows already covers the simplest cases for free.
notes: Espanso exists, is free, is cross-platform, and does most of this at the OS level · build only if you want browser-aware form fields.
prompt:
Build a local Chrome extension (Manifest V3) called "Snip" that is a personal text expander. No accounts, no server, no telemetry, no analytics.

Stack: TypeScript, Vite with @crxjs/vite-plugin, plain DOM for UI. No React, no CSS framework, no state library. Storage is chrome.storage.local only.

Core behavior:
- A content script runs on all URLs and tracks the last typed characters in the focused element (input, textarea, and contenteditable).
- When the typed buffer ends with a snippet trigger (user-defined, e.g. "/sig" or ";addr"), delete the trigger characters and insert the snippet body at the caret.
- Insertion must work for three cases: input/textarea via setRangeText plus an input event dispatch, contenteditable via document.execCommand('insertText') with a Range fallback, and React-controlled inputs via the native value setter trick plus a bubbling input event.
- Support these template tokens only: {date:FORMAT} with offsets like {date:YYYY-MM-DD|+7d}, {clipboard}, {cursor} for final caret position, and {field:label} for fill-in values.
- If a snippet contains {field:...} tokens, show a small shadow-DOM modal near the caret with one text input per field, Tab to move, Enter to insert, Escape to cancel. Preserve focus and caret on cancel.

Options page:
- CRUD list of snippets: trigger, label, body (textarea), optional site allowlist.
- Live preview of the rendered body with sample field values.
- Export and import all snippets as a single JSON file.
- Toggle to disable expansion globally and a per-domain disable list.

Explicitly out of scope: cloud sync, team sharing, mobile, conditionals, formulas, remote data lookups, keyboard simulation, Firefox and Safari builds.

Include a README with load-unpacked instructions, a documented list of known-broken site patterns (iframes, closed shadow roots, canvas editors like Google Docs), and a short note that Google Docs will not work. Ship a seed set of three example snippets. No .env needed since there are no secrets.
